items.stem:
60 members of a sports club were asked which of swimming (S), cycling (C) and running (R) they did last week.

32 swam, 28 cycled and 24 ran.
12 swam and cycled, 10 cycled and ran, and 9 swam and ran.
5 members did none of the three activities.
x members did all three activities.

parts.t: Work out the number of members who did exactly one of the three activities.

A member who swam is chosen at random.
Find the probability that this member also ran.

sols: Members who did at least one activity: 60 − 5 = 55.
Adding the three sets counts each pair-overlap twice and the centre three times, so 55 = 32 + 28 + 24 − 12 − 10 − 9 + x
Check the regions: S&C only 10, C&R only 8, S&R only 7; S only 32 − 10 − 7 − 2 = 13, C only 8, R only 7; 13 + 8 + 7 + 10 + 8 + 7 + 2 + 5 = 60 ✓
Exactly one activity = S only + C only + R only = 13 + 8 + 7
The choice is made from the 32 swimmers.
Of these, 9 also ran (7 who swam and ran only, plus the 2 who did all three).
ms:
M1 for 60 − 5 = 55 used as the union
